correctness.rationale: In every existing Hadamard order n>=4, the normalized defective matrix has an exact 2D/orthogonal-complement splitting; an analytically optimized probability weighting yields nuclear-norm lower witness gamma_n. At the same weight a positive definite X has B^T X^-1 B=X and constant diagonal gamma_n, giving matching complex Schur factorization upper bound. The n=2 case is an isometric sign row/column multiplier. All quantifiers, strict positivity, boundary and sharpness are addressed; checker replay supplies 521 finite supplementary assertions and is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Real Hadamard sign matrices are exactly extremizers of the n-by-n sign Schur norm sqrt(n). Flipping one entry is the minimum possible sign perturbation, so measuring the exact loss is a canonical rigidity question; the all-existing-order universal n^-3/2 decrement, Hadamard-class independence, and explicit orthogonal/Gram certificates are mathematically informative beyond the known n=4 table. No arbitrary parameter slice or routine isolated computation is relied upon.
